## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Devatāpañhajātaka* (Ja 350) is the tenth and final story of the *Cullakuṇālavagga*, concluding the *Catukkanipāta* of the Pali *Jātaka* collection [Fausböll 1883]. In the standard Pali commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the text is represented merely by a brief lemma beginning with the verse opening *Hanti hatthehi pādehīti* and a cross-reference noting that this deity's riddle (*devatāpucchā*) will be expounded in full in the *Ummaggajātaka* [Fausböll 1883; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].
Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this internal cross-reference, recording eight shared segments (totalling 479 characters) between Ja 350 and the sixth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0514a2), which contains the *Ummaggajātaka* commentary (the longest match spanning §0.4–1.4 with a similarity score of 0.95) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Chaṭṭho bhāgo) (Atk S0514a2) (§0.4–1.4 ↔ §2572_9–2574)
